exceptions.title: respects finalFocus when initialFocus points outside the popup
exceptions.reason: With `modal` set to `true`, the elements outside the popup are inert (BUG-4678), so `initialFocus` cannot focus an element outside the popup. The case `BUG-4678: keeps the initial focus off an inert element, and returns the focus to $name` tests this, and the return of the focus.

exceptions.title: moves final focus to trigger if initialFocus points outside the popup and finalFocus is not specified
exceptions.reason: With `modal` set to `true`, the elements outside the popup are inert (BUG-4678), so `initialFocus` cannot focus an element outside the popup. The case `BUG-4678: keeps the initial focus off an inert element, and returns the focus to $name` tests this, and the return of the focus.

exceptions.title: should not throw "Maximum update depth exceeded" when Suspense boundary is outside Portal
exceptions.reason: The case guards a render loop of React (issue 3695) while a `Suspense` boundary outside the portal waits for a lazy component in the popup. The portal of Vase UI renders its content after the mount, so a Vue `<Suspense>` around it does not wait for that content and shows no fallback.

exceptions.title: does not warn for a detached payload open in production
exceptions.reason: The case needs a production build. Vitest sets `process.env.NODE_ENV` when it transforms a file for a browser, so only the Node project can change it. The case `ignores openWithPayload() with no root and gives no warning in a production build` tests the same.

exceptions.title: keeps the root attached through Strict Mode effect replay
exceptions.reason: The case tests React Strict Mode. Vue has no Strict Mode.

exceptions.title: closes a popover opened during a nested dialog, not the parent, on Escape after the nested dialog closes
exceptions.reason: The case expects the focus on `<body>` after the nested dialog closes. Vase UI moves it into the parent popup (BUG-6037), so Escape there closes the parent. The case `BUG-6037: on Escape after a nested dialog closes, closes $name` tests Escape with that focus, and with no focus in a popup, where the popover closes as in Base UI.

exceptions.title: closes a nonmodal dialog on Escape from an inactive trigger inside a popover on every open
exceptions.reason: The case nests a Popover and a Dialog of the older popup code. Popover moved to the popup layer, and the two do not share a stack until Dialog moves to it. The change that moves Dialog to the popup layer ports the case again.

The scroll lock waits for no lock of another library: it has one count for each document, and the last unlock restores the page. A lock of another library and the lock of Vase UI each restore their own styles.

exceptions.title: should not close the parent menu when Escape is pressed in a nested dialog
exceptions.reason: The case nests a Dialog of the older popup code in a Menu. Menu moved to the popup layer, and the two do not share a stack until Dialog moves to it. The change that moves Dialog to the popup layer ports the case again.

surfaceAdditions.reason: With `disabled`, the portal element and its parts render in the place of the part, also on a server (`VUE-128`). Base UI has no such prop.
The part reads `disabled` for its state and for `useButton`, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the trigger, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

The part reads `id` to give it to its element, or a generated id when `id` is absent, so it is a declared prop. The popup names the `id` that the element has in `aria-labelledby`. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the title, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

The part reads `id` to give it to its element, or a generated id when `id` is absent, so it is a declared prop. The popup names the `id` that the element has in `aria-describedby`. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the description, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.
The part reads `disabled` for its state and for `useButton`, so it is a declared prop. Base UI reads it from the native attributes of the button, and `types.md` has no row for a native attribute.

returnTypeDifferences.reason: `Dialog.Handle` is the class `DialogHandle`. The declaration of the function names the class, and Base UI documents the same class by its name in the namespace.
